newsitem.title: USA: TV ratings negotiators reported near agreement.
newsitem.headline: TV ratings negotiators reported near agreement.

text.p: Television executives are close to an agreement with parent groups on revamping the TV industry's programme ratings system to include references for violence, sex and strong language, a senator said Tuesday.
Negotiations between the two sides are set to continue Wednesday morning following talks Tuesday at the headquarters of the Motion Picture Association of America.

Industry representatives have agreed to add the letters "V," "S" and "L" to their six-month-old system to designate sexual content, violence and coarse language, a source familiar with the talks said.
But the officials are awaiting formal letters from leading members of Congress and the parent groups that would spell out the system.
"I remain optimistic they will reach an agreement very soon," Sen. John McCain, R-Ariz., told a press conference. "There's no doubt in my mind. The question is when."

Parent groups and lawmakers had argued the existing age-based system -- which includes TV-14 for parents of children under 14 -- strongly cautioned that it did not go far enough and was too vague. It was introduced at the start of 1997.

Industry officials had faced a Tuesday deadline from members of the Senate who insisted the industry develop a ratings system that satisfies parent groups -- or face legislation that would require changes.

Industry representatives had broken off negotiations late last week after Vice President Al Gore urged the industry to include the V, S and L ratings. The National Association of Broadcasters, which is participating in the talks, called Gore's statement "unwarranted intervention."
The V, S and L designations would be added to the TV-PG, TV-14 and TV-M ratings. TV-PG refers to parental guidance suggested and TV-M refers to mature audiences only.

In addition, children's shows rated TV-Y7 -- suitable for kids seven and older -- also could receive an "FV" designation for "fantasy violence." Shows such as "Mighty Morphin Power Rangers" would be eligible for that rating.
